title: VipAct: Visual-Perception Enhancement via Specialized VLM Agent Collaboration and Tool-use

live_model.evidence: Appendix A: 'For main experiments, we use the gpt-4o-2024-05-13 model from Azure OpenAI API ... temperature to 0'; Table 2 row VIPACT (Ours): average 73.79; Zero-shot 63.74

prompt.location: Appendix J 'Prompt Design' (orchestrator initial prompt and three specialised-agent prompts)
prompt.note: zero-shot baseline uses the Blink codebase prompts, not printed here

claim.metric: accuracy (%), average over 10 Blink validation sub-tasks

data.source: Blink validation set, 10 sub-tasks (Table 6 counts: 135+120+124+150+130+139+143+122+172+133); MMVP (300 questions)

notes: VipAct is a multi-agent loop that also calls open vision experts (Depth-Anything-V2, SAM, YOLOv8, CLIP) and image-processing tools; re-implementation from the printed prompts is substantial. Simpler alternative: Table 2 zero-shot GPT-4o 63.74, but that prompt comes from the Blink repository.

resolution.plan: The 73.79 average needs the full VipAct loop: orchestrator and three specialised agents (prompts in Appendix J, Algorithm 1) plus Depth-Anything-V2-Small, SAM, YOLOv8 and CLIP ViT-B/32 tool wrappers with Python code execution; the wrappers' input/output formats are not printed, so the pipeline must come from the authors' code, which the paper does not link. Fallback if the code cannot be located: the Table 2 zero-shot row (63.74) uses the Blink codebase prompt, which the BLINK release ships as a per-item prompt field. Either way, gpt-4o-2024-05-13 at temperature 0, three runs averaged, over the 1,368 Blink validation items.
resolution.approximation: No repository URL in the paper; tool wrapper behaviour reconstructed from the description would make the agentic number only loosely comparable.
